card.name: Start of foreign personal names
card.fires_on: The first piece of a surname or given name, often Asian or Eastern European, right after a first name, initials or title, such as Kong, Meng, Kon, Mog. It also fires on a stray 'and' in archive notices.

modes.label: Name starts
modes.description: Opening piece of a foreign surname in author lists, officials' names or citations.
modes.example: Small KS, Hedman AK, Grunberg E, Nica AC, Thorleissson G,<< Kong>> A, Thersteindottir U

modes.label: Split names mid-text
modes.description: A name broken into pieces after a first name, with the rest of the name following.

modes.label: Archive notice 'and'
modes.description: The word 'and' in a disclaimer about outdated archived material.
modes.example: Archive material is no longer maintained,<< and>> some links may not work.

card.writes: It pushes toward name-continuing pieces like 'raud' and 'Ske' and away from money and currency words.
card.plain: It spots the first piece of an unusual personal name, usually a foreign surname, in a citation or news text.
